hypotheses.text: Microcephaly (HP:0000252) is present in the vast majority of MAU2-deficient individuals (at least 14 of the 18 patients, or >=77%) in the Parenti et al. cohort, demonstrating that cranial growth failure is a primary cardinal finding of CdLS7.
hypotheses.rationale: In the Parenti et al. cohort of 18 individuals, microcephaly is singled out in the abstract and text as a consistent major feature alongside short stature, while classic facial gestalt signs show wider expressivity.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. describe 18 individuals carrying 15 heterozygous MAU2 variants and report that affected individuals display a wide spectrum from classic CdLS to milder presentations, highlighting microcephaly and short stature as consistent major features.

hypotheses.text: The presence of classic facial dysmorphic signs (synophrys, arched eyebrows, long eyelashes) correlates with variant class in MAU2, being significantly more frequent in individuals with truncating/frameshift variants causing MAU2 haploinsufficiency than in those with in-frame missense/deletion variants.
hypotheses.rationale: Parenti et al. report two distinct MAU2-specific episignatures and diverging molecular mechanisms: truncating variants cause MAU2 haploinsufficiency and secondary NIPBL reduction (mirroring classical CdLS), whereas in-frame variants primarily disrupt NIPBL-MAU2 heterodimerization without severe loss of NIPBL levels.

evidence.text: Parenti et al. identify that in-frame MAU2 variants impair NIPBL-MAU2 interaction, whereas truncating variants lead to haploinsufficiency and secondary NIPBL reduction, accompanied by two distinct MAU2-specific episignatures reflecting variant-dependent consequences.

new_directions.question_text: What are the exact patient-by-patient numerator/denominator frequencies for congenital heart defects, limb anomalies, and gastrointestinal abnormalities in the Parenti et al. 18-patient MAU2 cohort?
new_directions.rationale: Ascaso et al. 2024 cite 56% heart defects in specific non-NIPBL cohorts; determining whether MAU2 probands carry structural cardiovascular or limb anomalies is critical for clinical distinction from CdLS1.

new_directions.question_text: Do the two MAU2-specific episignatures defined by Parenti et al. correlate strictly with cardinal dysmorphic feature severity scores (such as the international CdLS consensus scoring system)?
new_directions.rationale: Demonstrating whether episignature subgroups predict classic vs. mild facial gestalt will determine if DNA methylation testing can resolve phenotypic ambiguity in borderline MAU2 cases.
